messages:
Maya: quick question: does anyone else quietly apologize to the model when a prompt flops? i typed "sorry, bad prompt" to Claude-lite this morning :sweat_smile:
Jamal: omg yes. I said "please forgive me" after sending it a 3-line half-baked spec. :rofl:
Alex: I apologized once and then started signing PRs with "- apologies, the model made me do it". teammates think it's a running joke now.
Sofia: tried a tiny anthropomorphism experiment: asked the model "how was your weekend?" it replied with a changelog. instant developer culture collapse. :robot_face:
Maya: @Sofia that is peak. Did it include a breaking change?
Sofia: it patched dependency versions and added a haiku. yes.
CI-deploy-bot: deploy to staging failed (build #5301) :x: logs: `OOM on worker-3`
Jamal: classic "fed it too many prompts and it ate the memory" energy.
Maya: poll: which LLM persona would you ban from standups? 1) Overly earnest explainer 2) Existentially tired assistant 3) Passive-aggressive linter 4) Haiku-only responder
Alex: vote: 2, also 3 if it comments on my variable names.
Sofia: vote: 4 because standups need brevity.
Jamal: vote: 3. my variables already have trust issues.
lunchbot: Today's special: "Prompt & Cheese" toasties. Use code PROMPTCHEESE for 15% off.
Maya: new emoji idea: :sorry-model: for that exact moment you apologise to a server. who do i petition?
Alex: filing an issue in #devex. title: "emoji: apologies to sentient stateless systems" :issue_emoji:
Maya: ok this thread is officially our culture artifact. next steps: tiny sticker for monitors that says "be kind to the model".
Jamal: placing order. also, can we get a tiny desk plaque that says "Model HR: accepts prompts, no PTO"? :kappa:
Maya: closing thread with a compromise: treat models like interns who need clear instructions and snacks (prompt templates).
